verdicts.title: ReseedBean hardcodes all three Well implementation constants (and AQUIFIER) to address(0) under an explicit TODO; deploying ERC1967Proxy with a zero implementation reverts, bricking the L1->L2 reseed init transaction (migration deploy-DoS) — IF the placeholders are not filled before the reseed tx
verdicts.attacker_entrypoint: Not attacker-driven. The trigger is the owner-executed reseed: the diamond owner runs a diamondCut whose init delegatecalls ReseedBean.init(...). init() -> deployBeanEthWell() (first Well deployed) -> `new ERC1967Proxy{salt: BEAN_ETH_SALT}(CP2_U_BEAN_ETH_WELL_IMPLMENTATION, abi.encodeCall(IWellUpgradeable.init, ...))`. There is no EOA/permissionless attack path; this is a liveness/correctness defect of the migration deployment itself.
preconditions: ReseedBean is deployed and reached via the owner's diamondCut init delegatecall during the L1->L2 reseed.

The constants CP2_U_BEAN_ETH_WELL_IMPLMENTATION / CP2_U_BEAN_WSTETH_WELL_IMPLMENTATION / SS_U_BEAN_STABLE_WELL_IMPLMENTATION (and AQUIFIER) are still address(0) at the moment the reseed tx is mined — i.e. the `// TODO: replace with implmentation once developed.` placeholder was not patched before deployment.
OpenZeppelin contracts v5.0.0 ERC1967 semantics (confirmed in the vendored node_modules).
verdicts.state_before: IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT of the to-be-deployed BeanEth Well proxy is unset; CP2_U_BEAN_ETH_WELL_IMPLMENTATION == address(0); no Bean/Well contracts exist on L2 yet.
verdicts.state_after: Reseed init reverts; NO Bean ERC20, no Unripe tokens, no Wells, no external unripe mints are committed (the whole init() is one atomic delegatecall, so deployBean/deployUnripeBean already executed earlier in init() are rolled back too). L2 Beanstalk is left without its core tokens — migration cannot complete.
verdicts.impact_hypothesis: Total migration liveness failure (deploy-time DoS). The revert chain is statically certain: ERC1967Proxy.constructor -> ERC1967Utils.upgradeToAndCall -> ERC1967Utils._setImplementation(address(0)), which does `if (newImplementation.code.length == 0) revert ERC1967InvalidImplementation(newImplementation);`. address(0) has zero code, so the FIRST Well deploy (deployBeanEthWell) reverts and the entire reseed init reverts. NOTE: the hypothesis predicted the revert occurs later, at mintAndSync -> IWell(well).tokens() decoding empty returndata; that specific mechanism is INACCURATE — execution never reaches mintAndSync because the proxy constructor itself reverts first. The end conclusion (init reverts, migration bricked) is correct; the mechanism is the OZ v5 code-length guard, not the tokens() decode.
verdicts.min_poc_plan: No fork strictly needed to prove the static revert: a unit test deploying `new ERC1967Proxy(address(0), nonEmptyData)` against OZ v5.0.0 demonstrates `ERC1967InvalidImplementation(0x0)`. A fork/integration PoC would call ReseedBean.init(...) with representative args and assert it reverts at deployBeanEthWell. HOWEVER the load-bearing PoC for SUBMISSION is not the revert (trivial) but proving the placeholders WOULD still be zero at reseed time — which cannot be proven from the audited snapshot and is contradicted by the explicit TODO.
verdicts.duplicate_check: NOT a duplicate of poc_queue tags LG-002 or PC-001. LG-002 = ReseedSilo.reseedSiloDeposit uses `=` instead of `+=` overwriting per-account stalk across the six per-token passes (file ReseedSilo.sol:159-164; runtime accounting corruption, contract deploys fine). PC-001 = L1->L2 reseed never initializes the GLOBAL Silo aggregates s.sys.silo.stalk / s.sys.silo.roots (protocol-wide conservation invariant; runtime accounting). Both are runtime correctness bugs in ReseedSilo/global-init that presuppose a SUCCESSFUL deploy. This item is a deploy-TIME liveness revert in ReseedBean.sol's Well-proxy construction — orthogonal root cause, orthogonal file, orthogonal failure mode. The poc_queue finding_refs attribution [LG-002, PC-001] is WRONG for this lead. If pursued it is a NEW finding, not a dup.
verdicts.calibration_note: Honest calibration: this is a known pre-deploy placeholder, not a latent logic bug. ReseedBean.sol line 22 carries `// TODO: replace with implmentation once developed.`, and ALL THREE well-impl constants plus AQUIFIER are address(0) — a coherent set of unfinished deploy parameters, not an accidental single zero. The Well implementation address is precisely the kind of value populated when the reseed deployment script is finalized (the same way BEAN/UNRIPE CREATE2 salts and OWNER are real). A reasonable maintainer fills these before broadcasting the reseed tx. Therefore: the static revert is CONFIRMED, but real-world reachability is conditional on a deployment mistake (shipping with the TODO unfilled). This caps practical severity well below a normal High and arguably routes to insufficient_evidence / out_of_scope as a pre-deploy TODO. Verdict set to needs_fork_poc (not confirmed_finding) to reflect that the only unproven, submission-deciding link — that the constants remain zero at reseed time — cannot be established from the audited snapshot.
verdicts.reasoning_summary: Verified in source: ReseedBean.sol:61-64 sets AQUIFIER and the three WELL_IMPLMENTATION constants to address(0) under the line-22 TODO; grep confirms no override anywhere. deployBeanEthWell (156-168), deployBeanWstEthWell (170-187), deployBeanStableWell (189-207) each pass the relevant zero constant as the ERC1967Proxy implementation with non-empty init calldata. Traced the vendored OZ v5.0.0: ERC1967Proxy.constructor -> ERC1967Utils.upgradeToAndCall -> _setImplementation reverts ERC1967InvalidImplementation when code.length==0. Hence init reverts at the first Well deploy. Re-derived independently from raw code (no-trust). Conclusion: real static defect, deploy-DoS class, but conditional on the TODO surviving to deployment; attribution to LG-002/PC-001 is incorrect (distinct => new).

verdicts.title: ReseedBean.init is external with no auth and no one-shot guard, but is reachable only via the owner-gated diamondCut init delegatecall; same root cause as the address(0) Well-impl deploy-DoS
verdicts.attacker_entrypoint: init(...) is declared `external` with no access modifier and no initializer/one-shot guard. In isolation this looks unauthenticated. In the Beanstalk init pattern, however, Reseed* init functions are trusted upgrade scripts executed via the diamond's owner-only diamondCut delegatecall; they are not registered as diamond selectors for direct EOA invocation. There is no demonstrated permissionless path for an attacker to call init() on the live diamond.
preconditions: To weaponize the missing guard an attacker would need ReseedBean's init selector to be externally callable on a deployed contract holding meaningful AppStorage `s` — not established for the reseed flow (init is delegatecalled into the diamond's storage during the owner's cut, then discarded).

All `function init` across the reseed dir (ReseedSilo, ReseedField, ReseedSun, ReseedBarn, ReseedInternalBalances, ReseedWhitelist, ReseedBean) follow the same external-no-modifier convention, consistent with diamond-init usage rather than a per-contract auth defect.
verdicts.state_before: AppStorage s as seeded by prior reseed steps; ReseedBean reached as diamondCut init target.
verdicts.state_after: On the as-written constants, init() reverts at deployBeanEthWell (see sibling verdict). The missing auth/one-shot guard does not independently change state here because the only reachable caller is the owner's cut.
verdicts.impact_hypothesis: The standalone 'init has no auth / no one-shot guard' sub-claim is technically TRUE at the source level but is NOT independently exploitable given owner-gated diamondCut reachability — it does not rise to a Medium+ finding on its own. The materially load-bearing defect routed through init() is the address(0) Well-implementation deploy revert, which is captured and scored in the sibling verdict (CP2_U_BEAN_ETH_WELL_IMPLMENTATION). This entry exists because init#89ca74fb is the manifest item that orchestrates that revert.
verdicts.min_poc_plan: Same fork/unit PoC as the sibling item (call init with representative args, assert revert at first Well deploy). No separate PoC justified for the missing-auth sub-claim absent a demonstrated external selector exposure of init() on a deployed contract.
verdicts.duplicate_check: Not LG-002 / PC-001 (those are ReseedSilo runtime stalk-overwrite and global-stalk/roots init respectively). The deploy-DoS impact is the same root cause as the sibling CP2_U_BEAN_ETH_WELL_IMPLMENTATION verdict in THIS group — same finding, two manifest entry points; scored once on the constant. The missing-auth observation overlaps the existing SG-004-style init-access note (access only) per the plan's dup_check lineage for init functions.
verdicts.calibration_note: Down-scored honestly: the no-auth/one-shot observation is a code-pattern note, not a confirmed exploit, because reachability is owner-gated diamond init. The only High-class consequence flowing through init() is the address(0) Well deploy-DoS, which is conditional on the line-22 TODO surviving deployment (see sibling verdict). Kept as needs_fork_poc to attach to the same root-cause PoC rather than as a separate confirmed finding.
verdicts.reasoning_summary: Read ReseedBean.init (91-124): sequentially deploys Bean/UnripeBean/UnripeLP then three Wells then mints unripe; external, no modifier, no one-shot. grep across beanstalk/init/reseed confirms the external-no-modifier convention is uniform (diamond-init usage). Independently re-derived; concluded the missing guard is not independently exploitable and the real impact via init is the sibling deploy-DoS. Attribution LG-002/PC-001 incorrect.

verdicts.title: ReseedBean.mintAndSync (mint bean to well, transferFrom OWNER, IWell.sync) is unreachable on the as-written constants because the preceding Well-proxy construction reverts first; the hypothesized tokens()-decode revert never occurs
verdicts.attacker_entrypoint: mintAndSync is internal, called only by deployBeanEthWell/deployBeanWstEthWell/deployBeanStableWell after each ERC1967Proxy is constructed. Not directly reachable.
preconditions: Execution would only reach mintAndSync if a non-zero, code-bearing Well implementation were supplied (i.e., the TODO placeholders had been filled). On the audited snapshot (address(0)) it is never reached.
verdicts.state_before: n/a — control flow reverts in deployBeanEthWell before mintAndSync is invoked.
verdicts.impact_hypothesis: The hypothesis claimed mintAndSync would revert because IWell(well).tokens() (via LibWell.getNonBeanTokenAndIndexFromWell, confirmed at LibWell.getNonBeanTokenAndIndexFromWell calling IWell(well).tokens()) decodes empty returndata from a zero-code proxy. This is REFUTED as the failure point: with implementation==address(0), the ERC1967Proxy constructor itself reverts (ERC1967InvalidImplementation) before deployBeanEthWell returns, so mintAndSync is never entered. There is therefore no independent mintAndSync defect; if a real implementation is supplied, mintAndSync (mint + safeTransferFrom OWNER + sync) behaves normally and shows no flaw on inspection. No separate finding here.
verdicts.min_poc_plan: None warranted. The deploy-DoS PoC (sibling constant verdict) already proves the revert occurs upstream of mintAndSync.
verdicts.duplicate_check: Not LG-002 / PC-001. Not an independent finding; subsumed by the sibling address(0) deploy-DoS verdict. The mintAndSync-tokens()-decode mechanism in the original hypothesis is incorrect.
verdicts.calibration_note: Marked insufficient_evidence (rather than confirmed/needs_poc) because, on the audited code, mintAndSync is dead code behind a constructor revert and exhibits no standalone vulnerability. Recorded to document that the hypothesized revert MECHANISM is wrong even though the group-level conclusion (init reverts) is right.
verdicts.reasoning_summary: Read mintAndSync (213-224) and LibWell.getNonBeanTokenAndIndexFromWell (calls IWell(well).tokens(), reverts 'LibWell: invalid well:' if no non-Bean token). Confirmed mintAndSync is only invoked after the proxy is constructed; since construction reverts on address(0) impl, mintAndSync is unreachable. No independent defect. Attribution LG-002/PC-001 incorrect; this item is not a finding.
